verdict.rationale: Rootly documents an official MCP server that exposes incident data and actions to any MCP client. Its tools are generated from the OpenAPI spec, so they mirror the full API surface. Rootly also documents a REST API with role-scoped API keys that can create incidents programmatically. However, no evidence explicitly shows acknowledging, escalating, or resolving incidents through the API or MCP; the explicit acknowledge/escalate/resolve claim covers only Microsoft Teams. Missing for 10: documented API/MCP operations for acknowledge, escalate and resolve; an end-to-end agent lifecycle example; independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can acknowledge, escalate, and resolve incidents end to end through a documented API or MCP connection — no dashboard in the loop

citations.quote: The Rootly MCP Server implements the Model Context Protocol to expose Rootly incident data and actions as tools that any MCP-compatible client can use.
The server dynamically generates tools from Rootly's OpenAPI specification, so it always reflects the current API surface.
you can query incidents, check on-call schedules, find similar past incidents, and take action — all from within Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, or any other MCP-compatible environment.
The Rootly API allows you to create incidents automatically from monitoring tools, CI/CD pipelines, internal services, or any external automation system.
Global API Keys are assigned an On-Call and Incident Response role when they’re generated.
